title: Time and Space Complexity Analysis & Master Theorem
content: Algorithm efficiency is evaluated using Big-O (upper bound), Big-Omega (lower bound), and Big-Theta (tight bound). Key data structure complexities: Arrays offer O(1) access and O(n) insert/delete. Hash Tables provide O(1) average lookup/insert but degrade to O(n) during severe collision clustering. Binary Search Trees offer O(log n) balanced search, degrading to O(n) if unbalanced (resolved via AVL or Red-Black trees).
key_takeaways: Asymptotic notation evaluates growth rate independent of hardware
Space complexity must account for recursive stack frames
Hash table load factor determines re-hashing frequency

title: Graph Traversal & Shortest Path Algorithms
content: Breadth-First Search (BFS) uses a queue (FIFO) and discovers nodes layer by layer, guaranteeing the shortest path in unweighted graphs with time complexity O(V + E). Depth-First Search (DFS) uses a recursion stack or explicit LIFO stack to explore topological orderings and connected components. For weighted graphs, Dijkstra's algorithm uses a priority queue with O((V + E) log V) time, while Bellman-Ford accommodates negative edge weights with O(V * E).
key_takeaways: BFS uses queue for level-order and unweighted shortest paths
DFS is optimal for cycle detection and topological sorting
